entries.claim: With one seed per model, the z-mediated generator B1 (as implemented: absolute-map decoder, no path that copies s_0) has a dense error that is statistically tied with the direct generator B0 on TACO (1.732 vs 1.700; paired difference +0.031 [-0.009, +0.076]) and 14.1 % higher on ARCTIC (2.157 vs 1.890; paired difference +0.266 [+0.189, +0.345]).

Per-model intervals are unpaired 95 % take-cluster bootstrap intervals (1000 resamples); the comparison uses the paired difference mean(B1 - B0) on identical sequences with a paired 95 % take-cluster bootstrap interval. Report rule: better / worse only if the paired interval excludes 0 and the relative change is at least 2 %.

Report Section 8 disclosure: three of the four latent runs were stopped by hand before the protocol's 20 000-step minimum (ARCTIC B1 at 18 000, TACO B2 at 14 000, ARCTIC B2 at 12 000 steps), and the stop followed a preliminary test pass of the same step-4 000 states, so it was not test-blind. Checkpoints were selected on validation only and the preliminary and final test numbers are identical; a later validation best is not excluded, in particular for ARCTIC B1.
Unequal effective training length: B0 was selected at 79 000 (TACO) / 33 000 (ARCTIC) steps, all latent models at 4 000.
The per-model intervals in main_metrics.csv are unpaired and overlap on both datasets; only the paired difference decides the comparison.
On ARCTIC the z-mediated error (2.157) is close to the do-nothing persistence predictor (2.242); no paired test of B1 against persistence exists in the tables.

The comparison is confounded by design asymmetries stated in the report's limitations: B0 predicts a residual around s_0 while B1 decodes absolute maps without access to the Stage-1 encoder; the decoders read per-point geometry tokens B0's head never sees; B1 / B2 dense losses used 4 random frames per sequence per step while B0 used all 63.
Report Section 18 Q1 prints the ARCTIC interval as '+0.19 to +0.34'; the table value is [+0.189, +0.345].
Fixed ground-truth s_0 protocol only; TACO and ARCTIC only (OakInk2 is out of scope of this experiment).
entries.claim_as_extracted: Predicting the 63 future contact maps through the Stage-1 structure-oriented latent z (B1) instead of directly (B0) leaves the dense error statistically tied on TACO (paired interval includes zero) and makes it 14.1 % worse on ARCTIC (paired interval excludes zero).
entries.correction_reason: Values, direction and dataset scope are right. 'makes it worse' reads as a causal statement about the representation, while the report itself lists confounds of the B1-vs-B0 comparison (decoder reads per-point geometry B0 never sees; absolute versus residual output; 4-frame subsampling of the dense loss; checkpoints selected at 4 k versus 79 k / 33 k steps). State it as a difference between the two models.

entries.claim: On TACO the z-mediated generator is better than the direct one on four of the five structural / wrench error metrics, by 2.7-7.0 % averaged over the 63 frames, while on ARCTIC none of the five is better and the contact-amount error is 8.8 % worse.

Verdict: better / worse only if the paired 95 % take-cluster bootstrap interval excludes 0 and |change| >= 2 %.

The report's dataset explanation (TACO amortises the initial cost because contact changes a lot within the window; ARCTIC never recovers it) is an interpretation consistent with the persistence errors, not a tested mechanism.
One seed; hand-stopped latent runs (report Section 8).

dataset_differences: Dense error, B1 versus B0: a tie on TACO (1.732 vs 1.700; paired difference +0.031 [-0.009, +0.076]) but 14.1 % worse on ARCTIC (2.157 vs 1.890; +0.266 [+0.189, +0.345]).

Structural / wrench metrics, B1 versus B0: TACO 4 of 5 better (participation +6.7 %, centroid +7.0 %, normal +2.7 %, wrench +3.2 %; amount unchanged); ARCTIC 0 better and 1 worse (contact amount -8.8 %), the other four within their intervals.

Horizon: on TACO B1 is worse in the first 16 frames (dense 1.146 vs 0.806 at t = 1-8), level at t = 17-32 and nominally lower afterwards, and its participation error is lower from frame 17 on (0.175 vs 0.205 at t = 49-63); on ARCTIC B0 has the lower dense error in every bin (gap 0.54 at t = 1-8 shrinking to 0.16 at t = 49-63) and the contact-amount error stays higher for B1.

Persistence context: TACO contact changes much more within the window (persistence E_C 3.539, B0 1.700) than ARCTIC (2.242, B0 1.890); the report gives B0's gain over persistence as 52 % (TACO) and 16 % (ARCTIC). ARCTIC B1 (2.157) is close to persistence, and in the first bin it is above persistence (1.600 vs 1.345); on TACO B1 is below persistence in every bin.

Teacher-z* decoding floor (B1 decoder): 0.510 on TACO, 0.709 on ARCTIC; it rises along the horizon on TACO (0.40 to 0.61) and is flat on ARCTIC (0.63-0.75). Relative to B0 it is more than three times lower on TACO but less than three times lower on ARCTIC.
Initial-map detail the z path does not reproduce, ||D_z(z*_0) - s_0||: 0.382 (TACO) vs 0.541 (ARCTIC).

Latent predictability on the test set: mean per-dimension R^2 of the predicted z 0.487 (TACO) vs 0.349 (ARCTIC); test L_z 0.494 against a train-mean reference of 0.986 (TACO) and 0.510 against 0.829 (ARCTIC).
Share of test sequences on which B1 has the lower dense error: 48 % (TACO) vs 27 % (ARCTIC).

Frame-to-frame change: on TACO every model changes less per frame than the ground truth (0.315; B0 0.203, B1 0.157); on ARCTIC every model changes more than the ground truth (0.161; B0 0.186, B1 0.178, B2 0.184). The deviation from the ground truth is larger for B1 than B0 on both (31 % / 19 %).

Predicted r: the residual correction is 3 % (TACO) / 7 % (ARCTIC) of the z path's displacement from s_0 and improves 52 % / 56 % of sequences; only on ARCTIC does B2 get a 'worse' verdict against B1 (dense frame-to-frame change and its deviation, about 3 %).
Rule outcome: case B with best supported model B1 on TACO; case E with best supported model B0 on ARCTIC. No representation is supported on both datasets.

Training / disclosure differs by dataset: TACO B1 ran to 20 000 steps and ended by patience, TACO B2 was stopped by hand at 14 000; on ARCTIC both latent runs were stopped by hand (B1 at 18 000, B2 at 12 000), and ARCTIC B1 is the run for which a later validation best is not excluded. B0 was selected at 79 000 steps (TACO) and 33 000 (ARCTIC).

Sample size and interval width: TACO 364 test sequences from 186 takes; ARCTIC 186 test sequences from 44 takes, so ARCTIC per-model intervals are wide (B0 E_C 1.63-2.17) although the paired differences are not.

Against the previous direct model D0: on TACO B1 is still better on centroid, normal, wrench and the dense error (2-5 %), participation not distinguishable; on ARCTIC B1 is worse on the dense error (-9.8 %) and amount (-8.4 %) but better on centroid (+5.6 %) and normal (+4.3 %).
OakInk2 is not part of this experiment: every result in these blocks exists for TACO and ARCTIC only.
do_not_claim: 'z failed as a temporal state' or 'z is a bad state' -- the report states the opposite reading: the latent trajectory, if it could be predicted, would be more than enough; what is not supported is that z is an easier prediction target under this formulation.

'Z-mediated generation is better on TACO' without qualification -- the dense error is tied (nominally 1.8 % worse); only four structural / wrench metrics are better, by 2.7-7.0 %, and only at long horizon. 'Case B' is the rule's label, not a dense-error win.
'The structural benefit holds over the whole sequence' -- in the first 16 frames the direct model is better on dense error, participation, centroid, normal and wrench.
'B0 is 42 % better at t = 1-8' -- the report's figure is 'B1 is 42 % worse' (1.146 vs 0.806).
'On ARCTIC z-mediation is worse on every structural metric' -- only the contact amount is worse by the rule; participation, centroid, normal and wrench are within their intervals.
Any pooled or averaged statement across TACO and ARCTIC (for example an average percentage change of B1 versus B0).

'Decoding the teacher z shows what a z-based generator can reach' -- the teacher latent is computed from the true future frames and is unavailable at inference; it bounds what the representation and decoder allow.
'The teacher-z error is three times lower than any model' as a statement for both datasets -- against B0 it is less than a factor of three on ARCTIC (0.709 vs 1.890).
'90 % of the error is caused by latent prediction' as a variance decomposition or causal attribution -- the number is one minus a ratio of squared mean errors.

'The missing copy of s_0 is the cause of the gap' or 'giving the model the encoded s_0 fixes it' -- the report names this asymmetry as a limitation and did not test such a model; the stateful-z / s_0-preserving design is a motivated current hypothesis, not a result.
'z is disentangled from r' or 'z and r are independent' -- nothing here measures that; use 'structure-oriented' / 'structure information is concentrated in z'.

'r is noise' or 'r is useless' -- the result is that a PREDICTED r (not supervised against the Stage-1 r, at checkpoints selected at 4 000 steps) provides little additional information; r remains a realization residual / complementary dense detail.
'Adding r does not damage z' as a positive finding -- the report calls this test vacuous because the r pathway does almost nothing.
'z mediation makes trajectories more stable' or 'closer to the true temporal statistics' -- the deviation from the ground truth's frame-to-frame change is larger for B1 on both datasets.

'The results are robust across seeds' or 'all models were trained to convergence under equal budgets' -- one seed; three latent runs were stopped by hand before the 20 000-step minimum after a preliminary test pass; B0 was selected at 79 k / 33 k steps and the latent models at 4 k.
'The checkpoints were selected with test data' -- they were not (validation only; sanity check 13 passes); what was not test-blind is the decision to stop three runs.
'The comparison isolates the representation' -- B1 / B2 also differ from B0 in decoder geometry access, in absolute versus residual output, and in the frame subsampling of their dense loss.
'B1 beats (or does not beat) persistence on ARCTIC' as a tested statement -- no paired test against persistence exists in the tables (2.157 vs 2.242 are unpaired means).
'The larger direct model B0 is better than the previous D0 on everything' -- on TACO it is worse than the previous D0 on participation and centroid.

'The latent is harder to predict because of poor temporal geometry / because the future is stochastic' -- this report gives no test of the reason; it only reports that about half (TACO) / a third (ARCTIC) of the teacher's variance is predicted.

Any statement about human intent, robot null-space motion, 'contact does not move over time', or universal determinism from these blocks; the wrench profile is a proxy for functional grasp capability only.
Any OakInk2 claim: the experiment has no OakInk2 result.
